env.world: A finite observational experiment with a categorical confounder. One unit is the triple \(O=(X,A,Y)\) taking values in \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), where \([d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}\) with \(d\ge 2\), \(A\) is a binary treatment and \(Y\) a binary outcome. An observed law \(\mathbb P\) is described by its atom masses \(q_{ay,x}=\mathbb P(X=x,A=a,Y=y)\), collected into the four-vector \(q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x})\) and the table \(\mathbf q=(q_x)_{x=1}^d\); these determine the cell mass \(p_x=\mathbb P(X=x)\), the propensity \(\pi_x=\mathbb P(A=1\mid X=x)\) and the outcome regressions \(\mu_{ax}=E_{\mathbb P}[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) on occupied cells. For a fixed overlap constant \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is the class of such laws whose occupied cells satisfy \(\epsilon\le\pi_x\le 1-\epsilon\); the cell masses are otherwise unrestricted and null cells are allowed. The sampling model is \(n\) independent observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with common law \(\mathbb P\), indexed by \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The estimation target is \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a}\mu_{ax}\), the loss is squared error, and \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) is the infimum over all measurable estimators of the worst-case risk over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). The rate scale is \(L_d=\log(ed)\), and \(c_\epsilon,C_\epsilon\) denote the two constants of the frontier.

env.world: The four-cell analytic cone and the Poissonized pilot/evaluation construction. Write \(\mathcal J=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) with generic coordinate \(\jmath\), and for \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\) put \(s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1}\) and \(s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u)\). The overlap cone is \(\mathcal C_\epsilon=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^4:\epsilon s(u)\le s_1(u)\le(1-\epsilon)s(u)\}\), and \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is a globally Lipschitz extension to all of \(\mathbb R_+^4\) of the cell contribution to the target. Fixed universal numerical constants \(H_0>0\), \(0<\kappa<1\) and a cutoff \(D_0\in\mathbb N\) calibrate the Jackson degree \(K_d=\max\{2,\lfloor\kappa L_d\rfloor\}\) and the one-dimensional order-four Jackson kernel \(J_{K_d}\). An auxiliary count \(M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\) and independent fair marks \(B_i\in\{0,1\}\) split the included observations into pilot counts \(N'_{\jmath,x}\) and evaluation counts \(N_{\jmath,x}\). The pilot builds a random rectangle \(Q_x\subseteq\mathbb R_+^4\), the kernel builds the tensor polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\) on \(Q_x\), the centered factorial operator \(U_h(N;z)\) lifts monomials to unbiased statistics of the evaluation counts, and clipping produces the cell estimator \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\). Summing, projecting to \([0,1]\) and Rao--Blackwellizing gives \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\), which falls back to the empirical-ratio statistic \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\) on bounded alphabets. \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\) names the (open) sharp-constant derivation route attached to this construction.

env.world: The Poissonized moment-matching lower-bound experiment. \(\Delta_d=\{R\in\mathbb R_+^d:\sum_x R_x=1\}\) is the probability simplex, and \(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q\in\Delta_d\) are the two multinomial laws of the normalized two-sample distance experiment. The dense hard submodel is indexed by a contrast vector \(\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\) through the equal-mass law \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) with \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\) and \(\mu_{1x}=(1+\theta_x)/2\), \(\mu_{0x}=(1-\theta_x)/2\). For an even degree \(K\), \(E_K=\inf_{\deg p\le K}\sup_{|t|\le1}\bigl||t|-p(t)\bigr|\) is the best even-polynomial approximation error of the absolute value, and \(\nu_{0,K},\nu_{1,K}\) are symmetric probability measures on \([-1,1]\) whose moments agree through degree \(K\) with absolute-moment gap \(2E_K\). Setting \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil 4L_d\rceil\), \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\) and \(a_{n,d}=\sqrt{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}/(64\lambda_{n,d})}\), the scaled product priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d},\Pi_{1,n,d}\) on \([-a_{n,d},a_{n,d}]^d\) induce the two observation mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d},\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) when the total sample size is an independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\). Here \(r\) indexes the exponential likelihood expansion, \(L_{\theta_x}\) is the one-cell Poisson likelihood ratio against \(\theta_x=0\), \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}\) is the separation of the two prior means of the target, and \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\) is the minimax squared risk in that Poissonized experiment.
